name: sm_120 (consumer/workstation Blackwell) FP8 status: cuBLAS reports no FP8 path on SM_120 and CUTLASS ships no tensor/token-scaled FP8 grouped-GEMM CollectiveBuilder for SM_120
notes:
Verification of the parallel agent's claim: 'RTX PRO 6000 (Blackwell workstation, sm_120) has NO FP8 path in the current generation, and NVIDIA's own CUTLASS is unvalidated on it, requiring 12 upstream patches.' PARTIALLY CONFIRMED, with an important correction to how it should be worded. This source records evidence only; it is not a vendor spec sheet and carries no FLOPS numbers, so it must not be used to justify a throughput figure.
EVIDENCE 1 - vLLM issue 43507 (tgmerritt, NVIDIA, opened 2026-05-23, verified on real GB10/SM_121 hardware, still open): 'CUTLASS 4.5 does not ship a CollectiveBuilder specialization for tensor/token-scaled FP8 grouped GEMM on SM_120/SM_121.' CUTLASS 4.5 DOES ship SM_120 grouped GEMM for NVFP4, Blockwise-FP8 (per-block scales in the mainloop, example 87c) and MXFP8 blockscaled. What is missing is specifically the TENSOR/TOKEN-scaled FP8 (per-tensor dynamic scaling) specialization. The SM_120 dispatch policies exist in include/cutlass/gemm/dispatch_policy.hpp but are instantiated nowhere in CUTLASS - 'they appear to be placeholders for future work'. CUTLASS PR 3280 ('Add ptr-array TMA collective for tensor/token-scaled FP8 grouped GEMM', tgmerritt) was merged 2026-06-13, which post-dates this issue.
EVIDENCE 2 - FlashInfer issue 3255 (opened 2026-05-07, RTX 5090 = sm_120, CUDA 13.0): fp8 GEMM routed to cuBLASLt fails on sm_120 with CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED on real model tensor shapes. Diagnosis: 'cutlass_sm12x is the correct and sufficient backend for sm_120 - it handles all K values via padding.' i.e. the FP8 failure on sm_120 is a LIBRARY-ROUTING gap, not proof that the silicon lacks an FP8 tensor path.
CORRECTION - 'NO FP8 PATH' OVERSTATES IT. The evidence establishes that the FP8 GROUPED/MoE-GEMM path specifically is unpopulated upstream, and that cuBLAS's fp8 grouped path does not support sm_120. It does NOT establish that sm_120 silicon cannot execute FP8 MMA: the same CUTLASS release demonstrably runs Blockwise-FP8 and MXFP8 on SM_120, and torch._scaled_mm FP8 works on these cards (it is the documented fallback in EVIDENCE 2). The defensible statement is: tensor/token-scaled FP8 MoE is not served by NVIDIA's own kernels on sm_120 today and falls back to Triton, while NVFP4 - the precision NVIDIA actually markets these cards for - is the well-supported path.
THE '12 UPSTREAM PATCHES' NUMBER IS NOT CONFIRMED. No source found states a count of 12 required patches to run CUTLASS on the RTX PRO 6000. Do not record that figure anywhere.
WHETHER THIS IS TRUE OF THE RTX PRO 4500 TOO: not separately verified, and it does not need to be - all RTX PRO Blackwell workstation parts and all GeForce RTX 50 parts are the same sm_120/sm_121 family (the RTX PRO 4500 datasheet prints 'Tensor Cores 5th Generation', FP4 support, and no FP8 figure at all), so an sm_120 library gap applies identically to both parts. What is specific to each card is only its marketing FP4 number: 4,000 AI TOPS sparse for the 6000 versus 1,617 AI TOPS sparse for the 4500.
